summary: Create an orchestrating capability `src/modules/board/` that owns board policy (hide archived, group by status, attach visible labels, reject unviewable labels) and consumes only the trusted `server.ts` surfaces of `work-items` and `labels`. The board page is a thin RSC composition under `app/(app)/board/`, board's only channel surface is `rsc.ts`, and the label join is sequenced after item-id derivation with a complete visible/missing/forbidden resolution so forbidden labels reject the load instead of being silently dropped. Work-items and labels stay independently changeable: they gain narrow translated public contracts, accept explicit identity, stay silent, and never import each other or board.

tree.purpose: Pure board types (BoardCard/BoardColumn/BoardView) and pure functions hideArchived, collectLabelIds (dedupe + cap), groupByStatus.
LabelResolution type and assertCompleteResolution(requested, resolution) — the non-enumerating completeness invariant for the authorization-sensitive join.
Closed BoardFailure set used as typed expected outcomes: unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, contract.
BoardItemSource and BoardLabelSource role interfaces expressed in board language (itemsForBoard, resolveForBoard), owning board-facing types.
The orchestrating operation: filters archived, derives label ids, sequences the label resolution, rejects forbidden labels, projects the BoardView. Framework-neutral, silent, returns a typed result.
server-only private adapter implementing BoardItemSource by calling @/modules/work-items/server and mapping WorkItemSummary to BoardItem.
server-only private adapter implementing BoardLabelSource by calling @/modules/labels/server and mapping LabelSummary to BoardLabel.
server-only typed factory: RequestIdentity in, the smallest dependency object loadBoard needs out. Capability-local composition, no DI container.

server-only current-request surface getBoardView(rawParams): authenticates, validates untrusted params, wires the loader, maps typed failures to renderable state, and owns the single unexpected-error report.
RSC page; passes raw params to board/rsc.ts and renders the returned view state. Owns no product policy.
Route-private presentation for columns and cards; not promoted into board/ui because it is neither reused nor part of the capability contract.
Renders the failure boundary only; does not re-report an exception already reported by rsc.ts.
Route-level streaming fallback for the RSC read.
Existing trusted surface gains listBoardWorkItems(identity, { boardId }): WorkItemSummary[] — explicit identity, own policy rechecked, silent, archived flag exposed so board owns the hiding decision.
Existing trusted surface gains resolveLabelVisibility(identity, ids) returning a translated { visible, missing, forbidden } contract — complete and non-enumerating, no provider rows.

flows: RSC read: app/(app)/board/page.tsx -> board/rsc.ts getBoardView(rawParams) -> parse params with board's own schema -> requireActor() to RequestIdentity { actorId, roles, tenantId, requestId, traceId } -> createBoardLoader(identity) -> loadBoard(request, deps) -> typed failure becomes renderable state, unexpected exception is reported once then rethrown to error.tsx.

loadBoard: items = deps.items.itemsForBoard({ boardId, tenantId }) -> active = hideArchived(items) [pure] -> labelIds = collectLabelIds(active) [pure, deduped, capped] -> resolution = labelIds.length ? deps.labels.resolveForBoard(labelIds) : EMPTY (sequenced, never Promise.all, because ids derive from the filtered items) -> assertCompleteResolution(labelIds, resolution) -> forbidden.length > 0 returns { ok: false, failure: { kind: 'forbidden' } } -> otherwise groupByStatus(active, resolution.visible).

Item read: board/server/work-items-source.ts -> work-items/server.ts listBoardWorkItems(identity, ...) -> work-items private store/RLS with tenant and ownership predicates -> WorkItemSummary mapped to BoardItem in the adapter.

Label read: board/server/labels-source.ts -> labels/server.ts resolveLabelVisibility(identity, ids) -> labels policy decides visible/missing/forbidden -> LabelSummary mapped to BoardBoardLabel in the adapter; missing ids are omitted from cards, forbidden ids reject the load, and the rendered view never distinguishes the two.

Failure path: private adapters map provider errors to semantic failures without reporting; work-items/server.ts, labels/server.ts and loadBoard report nothing; board/rsc.ts reports the unexpected exception once with identity/trace context, marks it already-reported, and rethrows; framework navigation (notFound(), or forbidden() when authInterrupts is enabled) is invoked only after a typed result is known, never inside a generic catch.

decisions.choice: A new orchestrating capability src/modules/board/ rather than logic in app/(app)/board/page.tsx
decisions.rationale: Deleting the coordinating code would move archived filtering, status grouping, label-id derivation, projection, sequencing, and the forbidden-label authorization consequence into the route. The deletion test therefore mandates an orchestrating capability even with a single current consumer.

decisions.choice: Only rsc.ts; no server.ts, actions.ts, client.ts, query-cache.ts, stream.ts, or job.ts
decisions.rationale: The only channel required is an RSC read and the only consumer is board's own page. Surfaces are created only when a real consumer exists.

decisions.choice: board-columns.tsx stays route-private under app/(app)/board/, no board/ui segment
decisions.rationale: The presentation is neither reused nor part of the capability's public contract, and empty or speculative segments are forbidden.

decisions.choice: board/server/* private adapters call work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts; the two source capabilities import neither each other nor board
decisions.rationale: Keeps work-items and labels independently changeable, keeps the module graph acyclic, and lets board's application layer name its dependencies in its own language through ports.

decisions.choice: work-items/server.ts returns WorkItemSummary including the archived flag; board's domain hides it
decisions.rationale: Hiding archived items is board policy, not work-items policy. Pushing the filter into work-items would make board's presentation rule a shared lifecycle concern of another capability.

decisions.choice: resolveLabelVisibility returns a complete { visible, missing, forbidden } resolution; board rejects on any forbidden id and omits missing ids
decisions.rationale: The join is authorization-sensitive, so it requires a complete non-enumerating resolution. Silently dropping a forbidden reference would hide a policy violation; the rendered view still cannot distinguish missing from forbidden.

decisions.choice: Sequential item read then label resolution, no Promise.all across the two capabilities
decisions.rationale: The label ids are derived from the archived-filtered item set, so the second call depends on the first result. This dependent ordering is one of the few call mechanics worth asserting in tests.

decisions.choice: Typed result union out of loadBoard for expected outcomes; exceptions for defects and outages, reported once in board/rsc.ts
decisions.rationale: Expected application outcomes are typed values and each outer channel owns one translation and one report. Adapters and trusted server.ts surfaces stay silent so the report is not duplicated.

decisions.choice: Authenticate in board/rsc.ts; business authorization in board application plus each source capability's policy; tenant/ownership predicates in each source capability's store/RLS
decisions.rationale: Three-layer defense in depth. Board's trusted callees accept established explicit identity and never rediscover the current user through an auth provider.

decisions.choice: Route params validated in board/rsc.ts; provider rows validated inside each source capability; board only checks the resolution-completeness invariant
decisions.rationale: Validate untrusted input at the channel and provider data where it enters trusted code, but never re-parse a typed internal value because it crossed a directory. The completeness check is board policy, not re-parsing.

decisions.choice: No .from()/.rpc() and no store adapter under src/modules/board/**
decisions.rationale: Board owns no tables. Reading work-items or labels tables through string literals from board would breach the database resource ownership boundary.

decisions.choice: server-only on board/rsc.ts and board/server/**, plus path lint rules and a production build check
decisions.rationale: Path legality and bundle safety are separate guarantees; a Client Component importing a server surface must fail the build.

risks: board/application/ports.ts can drift toward mirroring the source capabilities' server.ts signatures. If itemsForBoard/resolveForBoard collapse into one-to-one pass-throughs, the ports have the wrong grain and the adapters become one-to-one facades.
loadBoard would fail the deletion test if archived filtering or grouping later moved into work-items; at that point board's operation should be re-examined rather than kept as a forwarding shell.

Label visibility is per-actor, so the board read must not be cached across actors. Any Next.js cache tag or revalidation wiring stays private in board/server/** or the source capabilities; no shared or actor-agnostic cache entry for the board view.

Rejecting the whole board on a single forbidden label is a deliberate policy choice; if the product later wants partial rendering, that is a policy change in board/domain, not a silent adapter-level omission.
collectLabelIds must cap and dedupe ids at the board boundary, otherwise a board with many items can turn into an unbounded batch against labels/server.ts.
If board's own report in rsc.ts is not marked already-reported, framework instrumentation can capture the same exception a second time; one capture owner must be chosen explicitly.

Adding a browser-driven board (drag-and-drop, live refresh) would need client.ts plus a GET Route Handler or stream and possibly query-cache.ts. None of that is built now, and it should not be pre-created.

A named re-export from work-items/server.ts or labels/server.ts is only acceptable while those contracts carry no provider row shapes and state their identity requirements explicitly; otherwise they need translated public contracts.
